questions.q: Which role is typically Responsible (R) for the day-to-day quality and definitions of one business domain?
options: Data Steward
Chief Data Officer
Database vendor support
End-user data consumer
questions.explain: The lesson identifies the Data Steward as the day-to-day custodian of quality and definitions for a domain — the Responsible (R) role in RACI terms.

questions.q: A job posting titled 'Snowflake Data Governance Engineer' is best understood as what, according to the lesson?
options: A platform-specific governance title applying the same underlying skills to a specific tool's catalog and access controls
An entirely separate career path unrelated to data governance
A role with no connection to glossary, quality, or lineage work
A title that only exists at companies that don't use any governance process
questions.explain: The lesson explains that platform-named titles (Purview, Snowflake, Unity Catalog, Fabric) apply the same governance skill set to a specific platform.

questions.q: Which earlier course in this path maps most directly to writing and automating SQL-based quality checks?
options: Data Quality Management
Master and Reference Data Management
Data Governance Program Management
Microsoft Purview
questions.explain: The lesson's mapping table ties SQL quality-check work directly to the Data Quality Management course.

questions.q: Per the lesson, what typically distinguishes a Data Governance Manager / Lead from a Data Governance Analyst?
options: The manager is usually Accountable at the program level, running the operating model, councils, and KPIs
The manager never interacts with stakeholders
The analyst has final sign-off authority over every domain
There is no real difference between the two titles anywhere
questions.explain: The lesson describes the Governance Manager/Lead role as usually Accountable at the program level, running councils, KPIs, and stakeholder communication.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what actually gets a candidate hired for a governance role, more than their prior job title?
options: Being able to show specific governance work — a glossary built, SQL checks written, a lineage diagram traced
Having a job title that contains the word 'governance'
A college degree specifically in data governance
Having worked at a Fortune 500 company previously
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly states there's no single governance degree, and what matters is demonstrable specific work, not the prior title.
